title: Wearing the Shoes of Someone Who Passed Away

chapters.title: Introduction and the Source in Sefer Hasidim
chapters.about: The question of using clothing and shoes of a Niftar and the teaching from Sefer Hasidim.

chapters.title: Customs in Baghdad and Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky's Remez
chapters.about: Practices in Baghdad, Hacham Ovadia Yosef's accounts, and Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky's reference to Debarim.

chapters.title: The Gemara in Hullin and Rationale of Sakana
chapters.about: Examining the Gemara regarding leather from an animal that died naturally and potential danger.

chapters.title: Rabbi Moshe Feinstein's Explanation on Contagious Disease
chapters.about: Understanding the prohibition through the lens of medical safety and sanitization.

chapters.title: The Gemara in Berakhot Concerning Dreams
chapters.about: Addressing the omen of shoes in dreams and whether it impacts the halakha.

chapters.title: Leather Shoes versus Non-Leather and Conclusion
chapters.about: Distinguishing leather shoes from slippers and non-leather footwear, and concluding on giving tzedaka.

summary: Rabbi Harari discusses the minhag and halakhot concerning what to do with the clothing and shoes of a niftar. He explores the source in Sefer Hasidim, the interpretations by authorities such as Rabbi Moshe Feinstein and Hacham Ovadia Yosef, and practical applications regarding giving items to tzedaka.
questions: Can you give away the shoes and clothing of someone who passed away?
Why do some people cut up or destroy the shoes of a Niftar?
Does the restriction on wearing a deceased person's shoes apply to modern non-leather shoes?
What is the source in Sefer Hasidim regarding the danger of certain items?
